headline: Germany intends to prohibit Cosco's 80 per cent stake in Zippel
what_was_said: Handelsblatt and Reuters (29 Sep 2026) report Berlin intends to prohibit Cosco's acquisition of 80 per cent of Hamburg logistics firm Konrad Zippel Spedition. A memo warns of strategic dependencies usable as leverage, and the review focused on software systems and sensitive data. Bundeswehr and NATO logistics are cited, and the Federal Cartel Office cleared the deal in February. The BMWE confirmed on 30 Sep only that an investment review is under way. No formal prohibition yet; Handelsblatt says a decision could come next week.

deal.target: Konrad Zippel Spedition (80 per cent stake)
deal.authority: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE)
deal.detail: Investment review under AWG/AWV; government reportedly intends to prohibit. Reported grounds: strategic dependencies usable as leverage in political upheaval; software systems and sensitive data; Bundeswehr/NATO logistics; transport infrastructure availability in crisis. Antitrust clearance February 2026. No formal decision as of 2 Oct 2026.

headline: Italy imposes golden power prescriptions on Pirelli–ABET HTS defence agreement
what_was_said: On 24 Sep 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a golden power decree, notified 28 Sep, on Pirelli's co-development agreement with ABET High Tech Solutions for remote-controlled electric rescue ground vehicles. It finds the defence activities strategically important and imposes techno-organisational prescriptions protecting IP, know-how, products, strategic data and R&D continuity.

deal.acquirer: Pirelli & C. S.p.A. (co-development agreement with ABET High Tech Solutions S.r.l.)
deal.target: ABET High Tech Solutions S.r.l. / Pirelli defence activities (cooperation agreement, not an acquisition)
deal.authority: Presidency of the Council of Ministers (golden power, DL 21/2012)
deal.detail: Techno-organisational prescriptions to safeguard industrial property, know-how, products and strategic data and ensure continuity and standards of R&D; detailed terms not disclosed.

headline: CFIUS clears BitFuFu's stake in Oklahoma bitcoin miner under national security agreement
what_was_said: CFIUS cleared Singapore-headquartered BitFuFu's acquisition of 51 per cent of Uni-Titan, operator of a 51 MW Oklahoma bitcoin mining facility, on 28 Sep 2026 under a national security agreement monitored by DHS and Treasury. The NSA restricts the site to specified crypto mining, limits certain advanced computing hardware and subjects facility changes to oversight. Notified December 2025.

deal.authority: CFIUS (DHS and Treasury as monitoring agencies)
deal.detail: National security agreement: use restricted to specified crypto mining operations; limits on certain advanced computing hardware; government oversight of improvements and equipment changes; ongoing compliance framework.

headline: Canada orders formal ICA review of China Union Holdings' Arizaro lithium deal
what_was_said: Lithium Chile announced on 29 Sep 2026 that ISED notified China Union Holdings of a formal review under section 25 of the Investment Canada Act of its proposed acquisition of Argentum Lithium, holder of the Arizaro lithium project in Argentina. CUH is reviewing the order; no grounds disclosed.

deal.target: Argentum Lithium S.A. (Arizaro lithium project; linked to Lithium Chile Inc.)
deal.authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (Investment Canada Act)
deal.detail: Formal review ordered under section 25 of the Investment Canada Act; grounds not disclosed; acquirer reviewing the order.

headline: Germany's draft Investment Screening Act enters inter-ministerial consultation
what_was_said: BMWE sent an 86-page draft Investment Screening Act to other ministries (reported 1 Oct 2026). It cites a considerably worsened security situation and targets Chinese influence. Reported points: listed-company stakes screened from 15 per cent, re-review on full takeover, EFTA states lose exemption. Reports differ on screening EU investors. No cabinet date.

headline: Mexican Senate passes national security review reform of Foreign Investment Law
what_was_said: Senate passed 65–30 on 30 Sep 2026 a reform adding a national security title to the Foreign Investment Law, covering acquisitions above 49 per cent in strategic sectors. CNIE expands from 10 to 13 ministries, adding Defence, Navy and Security. Tacit approval is abolished for security cases, with fines up to 200,000 UMA, about MXN 23.4m. Goes to the Chamber of Deputies.

headline: G20 trade ministers deadlock on overcapacity
what_was_said: G20 trade ministers in Milwaukee (1–2 Oct 2026) failed to agree on industrial overcapacity or forced labour; Greer called trade remedies inadequate; US has overcapacity investigations into 16 economies.

headline: China warns EU over discriminatory measures as France and Germany push tougher tool
what_was_said: China's Commerce Ministry said it would resolutely respond to discriminatory EU measures, after reports France and Germany are pushing for a faster, tougher EU trade defence tool against China.

headline: OFAC Iran designations hit automotive, rail, metals and shadow banking
what_was_said: On 1 Oct 2026 Treasury designated more than two dozen entities and two individuals in Iran's automotive, rail, metals and shadow-banking networks, with designees in Hong Kong, UAE, Turkey, Indonesia and Germany, and issued sector determinations widening secondary sanctions risk.

headline: Sycamore in advanced talks to sell Boots to Weston family
what_was_said: According to the FT (1 Oct 2026), Sycamore Partners is in advanced talks to sell Boots to the Canadian Weston family's Wittington Investments for around 9 billion dollars; a deal could come as soon as next week.

headline: Swiss consultation on Investment Screening Ordinance closes 5 October
what_was_said: Watch list: the Swiss consultation on the Investment Screening Ordinance implementing the Investment Screening Act closes on 5 Oct 2026.

headline: FSR in-depth review of JD.com / Ceconomy: provisional deadline 4 November
what_was_said: Watch list: 4 Nov 2026 is the provisional deadline in the Commission's in-depth FSR review of JD.com's acquisition of Ceconomy, where commitments have been offered.

headline: UK Supreme Court to hear LetterOne NSI Act appeal on 10 November
what_was_said: Watch list: on 10 Nov 2026 the Supreme Court hears LetterOne's appeal against the Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, the first NSI Act case at that level, on whether the forced sale of Upp required market-value compensation under A1P1.

headline: Japan's amended FEFTA rules take effect 4 January 2027
what_was_said: Watch list: Japan's amended FEFTA rules take effect from 4 Jan 2027.

headline: EU gives China mid-October deadline on trade imbalance
what_was_said: SCMP and Asia Times report the Commission has set China a mid-October deadline to offer ways to reduce its trade advantage, failing which it may unilaterally limit EV imports and tariff other industrial goods; Brussels also presses for an end to rare earth export restrictions. Sefcovic leads talks.

headline: UK reportedly preparing tariffs on Chinese EVs
what_was_said: The Times reported on 4 Oct 2026 that the UK is preparing tariffs on Chinese EV imports after the EU warned Britain could be excluded from its Made in Europe scheme; ministers reportedly weighed Chinese retaliation against JLR versus losing scheme access.

headline: China's rare earth export control suspension expires 10 November
what_was_said: Watch list: MOFCOM and Customs Announcement No. 70 of 2025 suspended the October 2025 rare earth export controls until 10 Nov 2026.

headline: Hindalco terminates AluChem deal after year-long CFIUS review delays
what_was_said: Hindalco and AluChem jointly terminated the 125 million dollar equity purchase agreement, citing extended closing delays beyond either party's control. Business Standard links the delays to the CFIUS review, repeatedly paused by US government shutdowns; no CFIUS outcome reported.

deal.detail: Parties cited extended closing delays beyond their control; press links these to a CFIUS review repeatedly paused by US government shutdowns. No CFIUS decision reported. Deal value 125 million dollars, announced June 2025.

headline: Schneider Electric to buy PTC for 22.6 billion dollars, expects CFIUS review
what_was_said: Schneider confirmed an all-cash 22.6 billion dollar deal for PTC at 205 dollars a share, expects customary approvals including CFIUS but no major issues, closing targeted Q3 2027.

headline: Germany prohibits Cosco's acquisition of Zippel
what_was_said: On 7 Oct 2026 the federal cabinet approved prohibiting Cosco (via Goldlead Supply Chain Development Europe) from acquiring 80 per cent of Konrad Zippel Spedition under the AWG/AWV, citing deepened dependencies and supply-chain resilience; formal notice from the Economy Ministry to follow. Cartel Office had cleared it in February; eight prohibitions to date.

deal.acquirer: Cosco Shipping (via Goldlead Supply Chain Development (Europe))
deal.target: Konrad Zippel Spedition (80 per cent stake)
deal.authority: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy; cabinet approval
deal.detail: Cabinet approved prohibition on 7 Oct 2026 under AWG/AWV: acquisition would deepen dependencies and endanger supply-chain resilience of Germany and the EU. Formal prohibition notice still to be issued.

headline: Šefčovič in Beijing on EU–China trade deadline
what_was_said: Šefčovič is in Beijing for two days of talks from 7 Oct 2026; Brussels wants product quotas and export curbs, Beijing rejected voluntary EV export restraints; Germany and France back a fast-reaction trade tool; EU leaders' summit expected next week.

headline: European Parliament adopts China report urging scrutiny of Chinese investment
what_was_said: On 7 Oct 2026 Parliament adopted its EU-China report 454 to 86 with 110 abstentions, urging closer scrutiny of Chinese investment in ports, energy grids and telecoms and use of trade defence tools; non-binding.

headline: Mexico screening bill reaches Chamber of Deputies; ICC Mexico seeks changes
what_was_said: Chamber of Deputies received the bill on 6 Oct and referred it to the Economy committee; ICC Mexico asked for four fixes (Proceso, 7 Oct); review asset threshold still unset.

headline: Šefčovič in Beijing; result due at European Council 15-16 October
what_was_said: Šefčovič's Beijing visit runs 8-9 Oct; he reportedly met Wang Wentao on 8 Oct; no outcome reported; EU leaders hear result at European Council 15-16 Oct.

headline: EU FDI Screening Regulation 2026/1386 applies from 17 January 2028
what_was_said: Watch list: Regulation (EU) 2026/1386, published 26 June and in force 16 July 2026, applies in full from 17 Jan 2028, with mandatory minimum scope and prior authorisation, repealing Regulation 2019/452.

headline: EU–China Beijing talks end with 'shared understandings'
what_was_said: Second round of EU-China Trade and Investment Consultations ended 9 Oct 2026: China to moderate hybrid and plug-in hybrid exports, cut MFN tariffs on almost 4 billion euros of EU goods, ease rare earth and magnet licensing; ministers reconvene by January, third round in March; Commission confirmation of joint statement unclear per Reuters.

headline: Wittington agrees to buy Boots for 8.9 billion dollars
what_was_said: Wittington Investments (Weston family, Canada), partnered with Fairfax, agreed to buy Boots UK and Ireland retail, Opticians, No7 and Thailand/franchise businesses from Sycamore and the Pessina family for about 8.9 billion dollars (6.7 billion pounds) including debt; close expected Q1 2027 subject to unnamed regulatory approvals.

headline: Treasury issues first civil penalty under Outbound Investment Security Program
what_was_said: Treasury announced on 7 October 2026 a 200,000 dollar penalty, issued in July, against Amidi LLC (parent of Plug and Play Tech Center) for failing to notify a roughly 92,000 dollar investment by its Chinese fund subsidiary in Noematrix (Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology) on 19 April 2025. Detected through Treasury compliance monitoring.

headline: COINS Act: Treasury regulations due by 13 March 2027
what_was_said: COINS Act, enacted 18 December 2025, expands the outbound regime; Treasury must issue implementing rules by 13 March 2027, and current rules apply until then.

headline: Commission publishes sixth annual FDI screening report: notifications up 40 per cent
what_was_said: Published 14 Oct 2026, covering 2025: 667 notifications versus 477 in 2024; 88 per cent closed within 15 days; 12 per cent needed in-depth assessment, 53 per cent of those in manufacturing; opinions in under 2 per cent of cases; all Member States now have frameworks.

headline: European Council 15-16 October: draft conclusions on China
what_was_said: According to Reuters via U.S. News, draft conclusions ask the Commission to continue dialogue with Beijing while using trade defence measures fully and adding new instruments; adopted text not yet seen.

headline: European Council on China: macroeconomic imbalances language, sector quotas, new instruments by year end
what_was_said: Euronews (15 Oct 2026): conclusions avoid naming China and refer to macroeconomic imbalances; leaders pressed for protection of chemicals and machinery incl. quotas; Commission to present a diversification instrument and solidarity mechanism by year end; further talks with Beijing in January and March. Seoul Economic Daily, citing Bloomberg and SCMP, reports a fast-acting tool that could cut Chinese goods off the EU market is to be prepared by year end. The 9 Oct arrangement allows 350,000 Chinese hybrids a year over four years.

headline: Treasury outlines CFIUS pre-filing consultation, risk matrix and Operation Shot Clock
what_was_said: In a Federal News Network interview published 15 Oct 2026, Assistant Secretary Chris Pilkerton described pre-filing consultation, a first public risk and mitigation list, escalation checkpoints within the 90-day review (Operation Shot Clock), the Investment Security Technology Initiative and the planned Known Investor Program.

headline: Poland opens investment control review of Skydance's indirect takeover of TVN
what_was_said: Ministry of State Assets opened proceedings under the 2015 investment control act after Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed; 90 days to approve or object; filing status disputed.

deal.acquirer: Paramount Skydance (indirect, via Warner Bros. Discovery)
deal.detail: Proceedings opened 14 October 2026 under the Act of 24 July 2015; 90 days to approve or order a share sale; TVN on protected list since end of 2024.

headline: Belgium's first FDI prohibition: NHV / GD Helicopter Finance; third annual report
what_was_said: Interfederal Screening Committee blocked GDAT-controlled GD Helicopter Finance's acquisition of NHV, announced 5 August; third annual report shows 191 notifications, screening phase in about 4 per cent; reasons unpublished.

deal.acquirer: GD Helicopter Finance (Dublin), controlled by GDAT Group
deal.detail: Minister cited national security, strategic interests and possible defence links; formal reasons not published.

headline: China's rare earth export control suspension expires 10 November
what_was_said: Suspension expires on the 10th of November.

headline: FSR review of JD.com / Ceconomy: provisional deadline 4 November
what_was_said: Provisional deadline 4 November.

headline: UK Supreme Court hears LetterOne NSI Act appeal on 10 November
what_was_said: Hearing on 10 November.

headline: Ireland proposes exemptions and shorter duration for Industrial Accelerator Act investment conditions
what_was_said: MLex reported on 19 October that an Irish draft compromise would let member states seek exemptions from conditions such as ownership limits, lift conditions after seven rather than ten years, and extend the rules to onshore and offshore wind technologies; officials discuss it on 26-27 October.

headline: China proposes adding 40 AI, biomedicine and solar technologies to export catalogue; registration in force
what_was_said: MOFCOM and MOST Announcement No. 48 of 2026 (16 Oct) proposes 40 technologies (23 AI, 5 biomedicine, 12 photovoltaics), 14 for prohibition and 26 for restriction. Pre-export registration applies from 16 Oct until the revised catalogue takes effect; comments close 15 Nov 2026.

headline: China extends drone component export controls to all destinations from 18 November
what_was_said: MOFCOM Announcement No. 49 (19 Oct 2026), one of four dual-use packages, controls drone motors, speed controllers, large carbon-fibre propellers and swarm/autonomy software for all destinations, previously US-only under Announcement No. 34 of August; effective 18 Nov; some agricultural drone thresholds relaxed.

headline: China's rare earth export control suspension expires 10 November
what_was_said: Watch list reminder: suspension expires on 10 November.

headline: Treasury issues proposed rule implementing the COINS Act outbound investment regime
what_was_said: On 22 Oct 2026 Treasury issued an NPRM implementing the COINS Act: notification requirements for notifiable technologies and prohibitions for prohibited ones. Covered areas are semiconductors, AI, quantum, high-performance computing, hypersonics and added biotechnology. Press reports name China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and Cuba and a 50,000 dollar threshold, unconfirmed from the Treasury release. Final rules to set the effective date; existing rules apply until then.

headline: UK Investment Security Unit clears OCS takeover of Mitie
what_was_said: The ISU cleared OCS Group's 3.1 billion pound acquisition of Mitie Group on national security grounds (Alliance News, 22 Oct 2026). The European Commission has also approved it; only CMA competition clearance remains, with completion expected in Q1 2027.

headline: China's Commerce Ministry condemns Treasury's COINS Act proposed rule
what_was_said: On Saturday 24 Oct 2026 China's Commerce Ministry, per The Hill citing Global Times, said the proposed outbound investment rule discriminatorily widens China-related restrictions, is an overstretching of national security, and reserved the right to take corresponding measures; officials urged the US to reconsider. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the aim is to stop adversaries using US investment to develop critical technologies. Public comment period precedes the final rule; no deadline found.

headline: Officials discuss Irish compromise on Industrial Accelerator Act investment conditions, 26-27 October
what_was_said: Watch list: per MLex, EU officials discuss on 26-27 Oct an Irish draft compromise allowing exemptions from conditions such as ownership limits and lifting conditions after seven rather than ten years.

headline: FSR review of JD.com / Ceconomy: provisional deadline 4 November
what_was_said: Watch list: provisional deadline 4 Nov 2026 in the Commission's in-depth FSR review of JD.com's acquisition of Ceconomy.

headline: UK Supreme Court hears LetterOne NSI Act appeal on 10 November
what_was_said: Watch list: hearing on 10 Nov 2026, the first NSI Act case at the Supreme Court.

headline: China's rare earth export control suspension expires 10 November
what_was_said: Watch list: suspension of the October 2025 rare earth export controls expires on 10 Nov 2026.

headline: Finland's government submits new investment screening act with greenfield coverage
what_was_said: Government proposal submitted 22 October replaces Act 172/2012; adds greenfield screening in defence, large data centres, energy and strategic raw materials, plus 66.6 and 90 per cent thresholds; intended in force 1 April 2027, subject to parliament.

headline: FSR review of JD.com / Ceconomy: provisional deadline 4 November
what_was_said: Provisional deadline for the Commission's in-depth FSR review is 4 November.

headline: UK Supreme Court hears LetterOne NSI Act appeal on 10 November
what_was_said: Supreme Court hearing on 10 November.

headline: China's rare earth export control suspension expires 10 November
what_was_said: Suspension expires on 10 November.

headline: China extends drone component export controls to all destinations from 18 November
what_was_said: Extended controls take effect on 18 November.
